key_insight: A mean-flow-based ROM can explicitly include Reynolds-stress effects in the equations of motion, improving turbulent channel-flow statistics while keeping the model low-dimensional.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate surrogate modeling route for CFD turbulence analysis and short-time prediction at moderate Reynolds number, with potential for higher-Re use cases.
method: Build a Galerkin ROM using modes from linearized Navier–Stokes equations around the mean flow.
Project Reynolds-stress divergence through a modified modal basis informed by the mean profile.
Compare controllability, balanced truncation, and POD-based reductions for statistics and forecasting.
evidence_signal: In a minimal channel at Re_tau ≈ 185, the framework matches DNS turbulence statistics and achieves short-time velocity reconstructions comparable to POD-Galerkin ROMs, with balanced truncation outperforming controllability modes.
watch_item: The approach depends on mean-flow knowledge and modified stress projection, so performance may be sensitive to model setup and may require careful validation when moving to higher Reynolds numbers or different geometries.
paper_title: Mean-flow-based reduced-order models of turbulent channel flow
